project.objective: Deliver a production-style, browser-demonstrable multi-tenant banking RAG knowledge assistant with inspectable grounded answers, reproducible local infrastructure, and executable evidence for each phase

acceptance_criteria.description: Architecture, phased delivery plan, setup, and explicit non-goals are documented
FastAPI health/configuration and React application shell build successfully
Reproducible container configuration declares PostgreSQL with pgvector, backend, and frontend services

tasks.outcome: A contributor can understand, configure, build, and start the standalone LedgerLens application foundation
tasks.title: Establish runnable project foundation

acceptance_criteria.description: Database migrations create tenant, user, role, document, chunk, and audit foundations with pgvector enabled
Authentication and RBAC enforce tenant boundaries in API and repository layers
Security behavior is proven by focused tests including cross-tenant denial

tasks.outcome: Authenticated users access tenant-isolated persisted banking knowledge according to roles
tasks.title: Add tenant-aware security and persistence

acceptance_criteria.description: Sample synthetic banking corpus contains no real customer data and covers core demo policies
Parsing, cleaning, chunking, metadata enrichment, and ingestion status work end-to-end
Chunks retain source, page or section, version, tenant, and authorization metadata

tasks.outcome: Authorized users can ingest realistic synthetic banking documents into traceable clean chunks
tasks.title: Implement document ingestion

acceptance_criteria.description: Embedding and reranker interfaces support production local models and deterministic test doubles
PostgreSQL pgvector and full-text retrieval results are fused with reciprocal rank fusion
Authorization filters are applied before results reach context construction and retrieval quality tests pass

tasks.outcome: Tenant-authorized questions retrieve relevant banking passages through dense and keyword search, RRF, and reranking
tasks.title: Implement hybrid retrieval and reranking

acceptance_criteria.description: Query understanding, rewriting, routing, context construction, and provider selection are modular
Answers expose citations, source locations, retrieved passages, latency, and confidence or grounding signals
Citation and grounding validators reject or clearly label unsupported claims

tasks.outcome: The API produces inspectable grounded answers with citations through a configurable LLM provider abstraction
tasks.title: Deliver grounded assistant answers

acceptance_criteria.description: Allowlisted read-only SQL retrieval is tenant-scoped and protected from arbitrary query execution
External or internal API retrieval uses typed adapters, timeouts, and explicit mock-demo integrations
Agentic retrieval decisions and validation are observable and covered by routing tests

tasks.outcome: The assistant can safely route suitable questions to governed SQL and API data sources and validate the combined retrieval
tasks.title: Add routed SQL and API retrieval

acceptance_criteria.description: Conversation history and semantic cache are tenant-aware with safe invalidation
Audit logs and request metrics capture retrieval and generation latency without sensitive content leakage
Versioned evaluation datasets and executable retrieval and answer benchmarks produce reports

tasks.outcome: Assistant usage is traceable, measurable, evaluable, and efficient across conversations
tasks.title: Add conversation, caching, audit, and evaluation

acceptance_criteria.description: The responsive React UI provides authenticated assistant and conversation workflows
Users can inspect citations, source passages, routing, scores, grounding, and latency
Admin views expose document ingestion, audit-safe operational status, and evaluation results with accessible interactions

tasks.outcome: Authorized users can ask questions, inspect answer provenance, manage ingestion, and review evaluation and system signals in a responsive browser UI
tasks.title: Build the browser demonstration experience

acceptance_criteria.description: Docker-based end-to-end smoke tests cover authentication, ingestion, retrieval, grounded answer, and browser delivery
Failure handling, health checks, configuration validation, and security-sensitive paths are tested
Demo runbook, architecture record, operations guide, and known limitations match actual behavior

tasks.outcome: LedgerLens runs reproducibly as a polished standalone demonstration with documented limitations
tasks.title: Harden the integrated demo
